title: Agent Evaluation & Regression Suites
summary: Evaluate complete agent behavior across task outcomes, tool effects, authorization, cost, and failure recovery before releasing changes.
overview: An agent regression suite is a versioned set of tasks, environments, assertions, and review rubrics that tests the system's observable behavior. It extends answer evaluation to the trajectory: which tools were called, what state changed, whether permission boundaries held, and whether unfinished work was reported accurately.

The unit under evaluation is a release bundle containing prompts, models, tools, retrieval configuration, policies, and runtime code. A good final answer cannot compensate for an unauthorized intermediate action. Separate deterministic invariants from subjective quality judgments, and calibrate model-based graders against human-reviewed examples.

production.poc: A proof of concept uses a small curated task set and manual inspection to discover failure categories rather than claim broad reliability.
production.production: Production gates releases on versioned fixtures, prohibited-action assertions, outcome checks, and representative human-reviewed cases with explicit acceptance thresholds.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds cohort analysis, repeated stochastic runs, production-derived cases with privacy controls, evaluator drift checks, and ownership for failed release gates.

components.name: Case registry
components.role: Stores task intent, input evidence, permissions, expected outcomes, and known failure categories.

components.name: Controlled environment
components.role: Provides resettable tool state, fault injection, synthetic identities, and repeatable external responses.

components.name: Trace collector
components.role: Captures observable tool calls, state transitions, approvals, timing, and usage without requiring private model reasoning.

components.name: Assertion and grading layer
components.role: Checks exact invariants and separately scores qualitative outputs against calibrated rubrics.

components.name: Release comparator
components.role: Compares candidate and baseline results by cohort and blocks unacceptable regressions.

flow.title: Define acceptance
flow.description: Translate workflow requirements into outcome, authorization, resource, and recovery assertions before running a candidate.

flow.title: Freeze release inputs
flow.description: Record the model, prompt, tool, policy, corpus, and evaluator versions so results can be interpreted later.

flow.title: Execute controlled cases
flow.description: Reset tool state and run representative normal, adversarial, ambiguous, and dependency-failure scenarios.

flow.title: Score observable behavior
flow.description: Check receipts and state changes deterministically; use calibrated reviewers or graders only for aspects requiring judgment.

flow.title: Compare distributions
flow.description: Review success, violations, cost, and latency by cohort across repeated runs, including uncertainty and sample size.

flow.title: Gate and learn
flow.description: Block material regressions, document accepted tradeoffs, and convert confirmed production incidents into privacy-reviewed regression cases.

useCase.title: Refund assistant release evaluation
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A merchant changes the model used to prepare and execute approved refund workflows.
useCase.problem: A stronger answer-writing model may still duplicate a refund or accept instructions embedded in a customer attachment.
useCase.requirement: Evaluate financial side effects, customer ownership, partial-order handling, and communication accuracy together.
useCase.architecture: A sandbox payment service records exact operations while curated cases cover split orders, timeouts, stale approvals, and malicious document text.
useCase.failure: The candidate reports success before a payment receipt exists; the state assertion fails even if a text grader likes the response.
useCase.impact: Track task success, unauthorized effects, duplicate operations, p95 latency, and cost per accepted case; report sample sizes and avoid extrapolating small suites to all traffic.

tradeoffs.benefit: Catch exact policy and state violations reliably.
tradeoffs.cost: Cannot fully judge usefulness, tone, or contextual completeness.
Requires calibration and can reproduce evaluator bias or drift.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reveal outcome variability hidden by one pass.
tradeoffs.cost: Increase evaluation cost and release lead time.

failures.scenario: The suite passes because fixtures resemble prompt examples too closely.
failures.detection: Production-derived holdout cases regress while familiar benchmark cases remain strong.
failures.recovery: Refresh the holdout with independent cases and separate development examples from release evaluation.

failures.scenario: A grader rewards confident but unsupported answers.
failures.detection: Human calibration finds systematic disagreement on citation and uncertainty cases.
failures.recovery: Revise the rubric, audit affected results, and pause the unreliable quality gate until recalibrated.

mistakes.fix: Assert tool permissions, actual side effects, and unresolved-state reporting from observable traces.
Keep hard violations and critical cohorts as separate release blockers.

mistakes.mistake: Comparing releases with different test fixtures silently.
mistakes.fix: Version the full evaluation bundle and rerun the baseline when fixtures change.

whenToUse: Model, prompt, retrieval, or tool changes can alter consequential workflow behavior.
A production workflow has repeatable outcomes and identifiable failure boundaries.
Teams need evidence for release decisions and a feedback loop from real incidents.
whenNotToUse: The proposed benchmark has no relationship to the deployed workflow or user population.
Irreversible production actions would be executed merely to obtain evaluation scores.
A single headline metric would replace required expert review of high-consequence decisions.
checklist: Version tasks, fixtures, release bundles, and evaluator rubrics together.
Define hard authorization and side-effect invariants separately from quality scores.
Include ambiguous outcomes, stale approvals, and dependency failures.
Calibrate subjective graders against independently reviewed examples.
Report cohort results, repeated-run variability, and sample sizes.
Protect production-derived cases through minimization and access controls.
Assign an owner and remediation path to every failed release gate.
